name: protobuf_peek
description: Read the wire structure of a protobuf message without its schema: for each field its number, wire type, absolute byte offset and full field-number path (3.1.2), with nested messages unwrapped. WIRE STRUCTURE, NOT MEANING: no field name, unit, enum or signedness is known without the .proto file; a top-level varint is returned raw with its zigzag reading (and its two's-complement reading where the top bit is set), a length-delimited field is a guess between a nested message, text and bytes (read_as, with also_reads_as for the other readings it could be). A message is checked as the encoding defines it: a varint is at most ten bytes, a field number is 1 to 536870911, wire types 6 and 7 do not exist, and a field that runs past its message is an error with its offset; a group (wire types 3 and 4, deprecated) makes the message unsupported and nothing after it is read. consistent_with_protobuf_wire_format means the whole window parsed, which a short or ordinary blob can do by chance. SENSITIVE: a string or bytes field can hold message text or a credential, so the answer prints a top-level varint and nothing else that holds a value: not the text of a string, not the bytes of a bytes field, not a number under a length-delimited field (the bytes of a string or token now and then parse as a nested message, and their numbers are its content), not a fixed-width value (raw bytes); each has its offset, length and reading and a finding id. A length-delimited field whose bytes are printable text is text, never a nested message (a nested reading of a string would show its characters as field numbers, wire types and lengths); any other is read as a nested message only when it parses whole, has at least two fields, writes every varint in its shortest form, orders its field numbers ascending and keeps them at 300 or below (random bytes pass about once in 3,300; real Biome messages 17,871 times in 17,872). A binary value that does parse that way shows that structure, derived from its bytes (rare for a key or a token, not impossible), with its numbers withheld; its payload as a whole is written to the values file on request (kind bytes, with payload_offset), so nobody needs to aim a window at it. A window is held to the same rule: aimed at the payload of a field this tool withheld it is that payload, so rows, field numbers and varints are printed only for a window that is a message of at least eight bytes that meets the rule; any other gets a status (not_accepted) and counts, no row and no number in its reason, and its diagnosis is in the values file on request. Those values are written only on write_values: true, in a job run with secret_output: true, to $OUT/protobuf-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, refused if it exists; refused outside a job). hex puts the message in the call, and a call is recorded in the trace: use a path for anything that may be sensitive (hex is limited to 64 KiB). Only a bounded window is read (length, default 8 MiB, at most 64 MiB): what lies past it is counted and next_offset says where to continue. Memory follows the window, not its depth. Budgets: max_depth (default 6, at most 32), max_fields including those tried as a nested message (default 100000, at most 500000) and max_seconds (default 60, at most 90); a budget that ends the parse is reported (partial, with resume_offset where to continue), and fields the depth budget kept from being tried as nested messages are counted (fields_not_tried_as_nested_at_max_depth), never silent. A path that is not a regular file (a named pipe) is refused. There is no universal protobuf signature, so this tool declares no automatic file match.

path.description: A file holding one protobuf message (or a message at `offset` in it)

hex.description: The message as hexadecimal instead of a file (at most 64 KiB; the call, and so the message, is recorded in the trace)

offset.description: Start decoding at this byte offset of the file (offsets in the answer are absolute)

length.description: Bytes to decode from offset (default: up to 8 MiB; at most 64 MiB); the answer says what lies after the window

max_depth.description: How deep to try fields as nested messages (default 6, at most 32)

max_fields.description: Fields to parse, tentative nested readings included (default 100000, at most 500000)

max_seconds.description: Stop parsing after this long (default 60, at most 90)

limit.description: Fields in the inline answer (default 200, and at most 1 MiB of rows); the whole list is in the file the answer names

write_values.description: Write the text of string fields, the hexadecimal of bytes fields and of the payload of a field read as a nested message, the numbers under a length-delimited field, and the diagnosis of a window not accepted, to $OUT/protobuf-values.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the answer never carries them
